quizzes.title: New York DMV All Chapters Practice Test — 50 Questions
quizzes.description: 50 real questions covering the full New York State Driver's Manual — signs and signals, expressway driving, passing, alcohol and drugs, right-of-way, school buses, and more. Modeled on the official NY DMV all-chapters quiz.

questions.question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, you should:
options: Race the motor to warn the children
Sound the horn so the children hear you
Walk to the back of the car to check the way is clear
Tell the children to stay away
questions.explanation: Never assume children have moved — walk to the rear of the vehicle to make sure the path is clear before backing out.

questions.question: Why is expressway driving different from ordinary street driving?
options: You must think faster and handle your vehicle more effectively
Trucks must go slower on expressways
There is more tendency to exceed the speed limit
There is more tendency to tailgate
questions.explanation: Higher expressway speeds mean less time to react, so you must think and handle your vehicle more effectively than on ordinary streets.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on an expressway, you should:
options: Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit
Drive to the next exit and leave the expressway there
Make a U-turn at the nearest emergency turn area
Make a U-turn at the next service area
questions.explanation: Never back up or make a U-turn on an expressway — continue to the next exit.

questions.question: What is the effect of combining alcohol and another drug?
options: It increases the effects of both
It has no effect on driving ability
It reduces the effects of the drug or medicine
It reduces the effects of the alcohol
questions.explanation: Combining alcohol with another drug often multiplies the impairing effects of both.

questions.question: After leaving an expressway and starting to drive on an ordinary highway, you should:
options: Check your tire pressure
Check your speedometer to keep at the lower speed limit
Stay twice as far behind other cars
Change your speed gradually to the lower speed limit
questions.explanation: High expressway speeds distort your sense of speed — check your speedometer to make sure you've actually slowed to the lower limit.

questions.question: A stop sign means:
options: Slow down if cars are approaching
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe to do so
Proceed carefully, you don't always have to stop
Stop only for traffic on the intersecting road
questions.explanation: A stop sign always requires a complete stop, then proceeding only when it's safe.

questions.question: You must pull over to the right and stop for:
options: Vehicles with blue, green, or amber lights
An authorized emergency vehicle responding with lights and siren
A hazard vehicle parked or stopped on the highway
Stopped or standing school buses
questions.explanation: When an authorized emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield, pull to the right edge of the road, and stop until it passes.

questions.question: A "slippery when wet" sign means:
options: Don't drink if you are driving
The road may be slippery when wet
The road curves ahead
You are approaching a hill
questions.explanation: This warning sign means the road surface may be slippery when wet — slow down and increase following distance.

questions.question: What is always true about road rage?
options: There is nothing a driver can do to prevent it
You must hold your position in the travel lane
Only violent people experience it
You should remain polite to an aggressive driver
questions.explanation: Staying calm and polite, even toward an aggressive driver, is the safest way to avoid escalating a confrontation.

questions.question: Seat belts can be most effective as injury-preventing devices when they are worn by:
options: The person driving the car
Passengers on a long drive
All occupants on an expressway
Passengers and the driver whenever they are in the car
questions.explanation: Seat belts protect best when every occupant wears one on every trip, not just on highways or long drives.

questions.question: You want to make a left turn at a green light, but oncoming traffic is heavy. You should:
options: Use the next intersection instead
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear
Wait in the center of the intersection for a safe gap
Take the right-of-way since you have a green light
questions.explanation: Pull into the intersection and wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic before completing the turn.

questions.question: A traffic light with a green arrow and a red light means:
options: Drive straight ahead only
Drive only in the direction of the green arrow
Wait for the light to turn green
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop
questions.explanation: A green arrow lets you go only in the direction it points, even though the main signal is red.

questions.question: Driving in heavy fog during the day requires:
options: Headlights off
Parking lights on
Headlights on low beam
Headlights on high beam
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog — high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility further.

questions.question: The car behind you begins to pass. You should:
options: Maintain your speed for smooth traffic flow
Pull right and stop so he can pass
Slow down slightly but stay in your lane
Blow your horn to allow him to pass
questions.explanation: Hold a steady speed in your lane so the passing driver can judge distance and complete the pass safely.

questions.question: On a New York highway with no posted speed limit, the fastest legal speed is:
options: 50 mph
55 mph
60 mph
65 mph
questions.explanation: New York's default speed limit on any road without a posted limit is 55 mph.

questions.question: A work zone sign is:
options: A white rectangle with black letters
An orange diamond with black letters
A green rectangle with white letters
A yellow circle with black letters
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange diamonds with black letters or symbols, warning of construction or maintenance ahead.

questions.question: After you have passed a car, you should return to the right lane when you:
options: See the front bumper of the other car in your mirror
Put your turn signal on
Turn your headlights on
See the other car's headlights come on
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see the front bumper of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before signaling back into the lane.

questions.question: What are the colors of warning signs for hazards ahead, such as curves or narrow bridges?
options: Black letters on a white background
Black letters on a yellow background
White letters on a blue background
White letters on a green background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow diamonds with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:
options: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully — a full stop is not required.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn. You should:
options: Signal and keep your wheels turned toward the left
Signal and keep your wheels pointed straight ahead
Flash your headlights so a driver will let you through
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you
questions.explanation: Keep your front wheels straight while waiting — if hit from behind with wheels turned, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor, you should first:
options: Try to pump it to build up pressure
Shift to neutral and shut the engine off
Try to raise it by hooking your toe under it
Apply the parking brake hard
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal rapidly to try to build up hydraulic pressure before resorting to the parking brake.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you should:
options: Blow your horn to warn other cars
Stop with part of the car on the roadway to warn traffic
Drive out fast to merge smoothly
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic
questions.explanation: Drivers entering a road from a driveway or private road must yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.

questions.question: The road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line on your side. You may pass:
options: Only in an emergency
Only if you are on an expressway
If traffic is clear
Only at an intersection
questions.explanation: On the broken-line side of a solid/broken yellow pair, you may pass when it's safe and won't interfere with traffic.

questions.question: A blind person legally has the right-of-way when crossing the street when:
options: Wearing light-colored clothing
Led by a guide dog or using a white or metallic cane
Helped by another person
Wearing dark-colored glasses
questions.explanation: A pedestrian using a guide dog or a white/metallic cane has the legal right-of-way when crossing.

questions.question: What are the consequences that can result from driving under the influence of alcohol or other drugs?
options: Possible imprisonment
A mandatory fine
Driver license revocation
All of these choices
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence can bring imprisonment, fines, and license revocation — all of the above.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle on the right if it is waiting to:
options: Turn right
Turn left
Park at the curb
Turn into a driveway on the right
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is stopped or slowing to make a left turn.

questions.question: A "divided highway ends" sign means:
options: Divided highway ahead
One-way traffic ahead
Four-lane highway ahead
The divided highway ends
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the physical median or divider is about to end.

questions.question: You may park in a space reserved for people with disabilities if your vehicle displays disabled plates or a permit:
options: Regardless of who is in the vehicle
Only if the driver is disabled
Only if you are carrying the disabled person named on the registration
If someone in your immediate family is disabled
questions.explanation: A vehicle displaying valid disability plates or a permit may use the space regardless of who is in the vehicle at the time.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither one
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Minimum speed signs are designed to:
options: Keep traffic flowing smoothly
Show current road conditions
Test future traffic signal needs
Assure pedestrian safety
questions.explanation: Minimum speed limits exist to keep slow-moving vehicles from blocking the normal flow of traffic.

questions.question: A "no stopping" sign means you may stop only:
options: Long enough to unload packages
To avoid conflict with other traffic
To discharge passengers
For less than 5 minutes
questions.explanation: A No Stopping sign prohibits stopping for any reason except to avoid a conflict with other traffic.

questions.question: A "right lane ends, keep left" sign means:
options: Merging traffic from the right
Winding road ahead
The right lane ends and you must stay left
Divided highway ahead
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane is ending and you must merge left.

questions.question: To overtake and pass a vehicle, you should:
options: Wait for a signal from the other driver
Change lanes quickly
Signal and pass only when it's safe
Stay close behind to shorten passing time
questions.explanation: Always signal your intent and pass only when you can see it's safe to do so.

questions.question: The best way to stop on a slippery road is to:
options: Apply the brakes quickly and firmly
Apply the brakes slowly and steadily
Shift to a lower gear and avoid the brakes
Shift to neutral and avoid the brakes
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes slowly and steadily on a slippery surface to avoid triggering a skid.

questions.question: What applies to all driving emergencies?
options: Always slow down gradually
Your first reaction is always the best reaction
Think before you act
Apply the brakes immediately
questions.explanation: Don't panic — take a moment to think through the safest response before acting in any emergency.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped ahead with red lights flashing. You:
options: May pass if there are no children near the road
Cannot pass while the red lights are flashing
May pass if you are facing the front of the bus
May pass if you are on the other side of a divided highway
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and may not proceed until the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?
options: Drinking coffee before driving
Riding home with a friend who has not been drinking
Taking a cold shower before driving
Stopping drinking half an hour before you drive
questions.explanation: Coffee and cold showers don't lower blood alcohol content — the only safe option is to ride with someone who hasn't been drinking.

questions.question: A stop sign means:
options: Slow down if cars are approaching
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe to do so
Proceed carefully, you don't always have to stop
Stop only for intersecting traffic
questions.explanation: A stop sign always requires a complete stop before proceeding when it's safe.

questions.question: A yield sign means:
options: Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is approaching
Look both ways before crossing the intersection
Always come to a full stop
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary
questions.explanation: A Yield sign means slow down and be ready to stop if needed to let other traffic go first.

questions.question: What effect does combining alcohol with a prescription or over-the-counter medicine have?
options: The medicine reduces the alcohol's effect
The alcohol helps the medicine work better
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol
There is no effect, since they are different substances
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine can multiply the impairing effects of the alcohol.

questions.question: Alcohol affects:
options: Recovery from headlight glare
Reaction time
Judgment of distances
All of these choices
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs glare recovery, reaction time, and distance judgment — all of these choices.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:
options: Always come to a full stop
Look both ways as you cross
Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is approaching
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary
questions.explanation: A yield sign (red and white triangle) means slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does a "slow moving vehicle" emblem look like?
options: A square red sign
A round green sign
A diamond-shaped yellow sign
A triangular orange sign
questions.explanation: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is a fluorescent orange triangle with a red reflective border.

questions.question: Driving in a state of rage can:
options: Affect your ability to reason and make decisions
Increase your chance of a traffic accident
Lead to a revoked or suspended license
All of these choices
questions.explanation: Road rage clouds judgment, raises crash risk, and can lead to license suspension — all of these choices.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to reduce your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
options: Drinking coffee
Exercising
Allowing your body time to eliminate the alcohol
Taking a cold shower
questions.explanation: Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower blood alcohol content — only time allows your body to eliminate the alcohol.

questions.question: A rectangular-shaped sign is a:
options: Speed limit sign
School crossing sign
Stop sign
Railroad crossing sign
questions.explanation: Regulation signs, including speed limit signs, are normally rectangular.

questions.question: You are making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street. When you complete the turn, your car should be in:
options: The right lane of the street
The center of the street
The left lane of the street
The lane with the least traffic
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should end up in the left lane of that street.

questions.question: In which situation is passing always forbidden?
options: The vehicle ahead is making a left turn
You are on a one-way street with two lanes
The vehicle ahead is stopped for a pedestrian in a crosswalk
The vehicle ahead is about to parallel park
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle that has stopped to let a pedestrian cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: A "no U-turn" sign means:
options: No left turn
No stopping
No U-turn
Detour ahead
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign simply prohibits making a U-turn at that location.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: Turn on the car radio
Slow down for better reaction time
Stop at regular intervals for rest
Move your eyes side to side while driving
questions.explanation: Plan frequent rest stops on long trips — that's the only reliable way to fight driver fatigue.

quizzes.title: New York DMV Chapter 4 Practice Test — Traffic Control
quizzes.description: 18 real questions from the official New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 4: Traffic Control — signs, traffic signals, pavement markings, and traffic officers.
quizzes.category: New York DMV — Chapter 4: Traffic Control

questions.question: A traffic light which has a green arrow and a red light means that:
options: You may only drive straight ahead
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow
You must wait for a green light
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop
questions.explanation: If a green arrow is shown with a red light, you may go toward the arrow, but only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. Your best action would be to:
options: Speed up to beat the red light
Apply the brakes sharply to stop
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection
Be prepared to stop before the intersection
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red — be prepared to stop before the intersection, not speed up or slam the brakes.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white (or yellow) line:
options: When to do so would interfere with traffic
When turning left into a driveway
When the car in front is disabled
When passing to the right on a one-way street
questions.explanation: A single broken line allows passing or changing lanes only when it can be done safely, without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign (stop sign) mean?
options: Slow down and prepare to stop only if cars are approaching you
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe to do so
Proceed carefully through the intersection, not always stopping
Stop only for traffic on an intersecting road
questions.explanation: A stop sign requires a full stop, yielding the right-of-way, then proceeding only when it's safe.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants in toward your left. This shows that:
options: There is an intersection just ahead
You are approaching a construction area
You will be required to turn left just ahead
The road will get narrower
questions.explanation: An edge line that angles toward the center of the road warns that the road narrows ahead.

questions.question: When the road is marked with a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line on your side you may pass:
options: Only in an emergency
If you are on an expressway
If traffic is clear
Only at an intersection
questions.explanation: On the broken-line side of a solid/broken yellow line pair, you may pass if it's safe and won't interfere with traffic.

questions.question: What are the colors of the warning signs that indicate hazards ahead, such as curves in the road or narrow bridges?
options: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow and diamond-shaped, with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: You may cross a single solid white line in the highway:
options: Whenever you want to
If traffic conditions require
Only to turn into a driveway
Only to make a u-turn
questions.explanation: A single solid line allows passing or changing lanes only when obstructions or traffic conditions make it necessary.

questions.question: A rectangular-shaped sign is a:
options: Stop sign
Speed limit sign
Railroad crossing sign
School crossing sign
questions.explanation: Regulation signs, like speed limit signs, are normally white rectangles with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: You come to an intersection which has a flashing red light. You should:
options: Come to a full stop, then go when safe to do so
Stop only if cars are approaching the intersection
Stop only if cars are already in the intersection
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it's safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Pavement arrows show which lane you must be in before you reach the line separating lanes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
options: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive with caution — it does not require a stop.

questions.question: What are the colors of a sign which tells you the distance to the next exit of a highway?
options: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Destination signs, which show direction and distance to locations, are green with white letters.

questions.question: You may cross a double solid yellow line:
options: To pass a slow moving truck
To turn into a driveway
To pass a car if traffic permits
Under no conditions
questions.explanation: Double solid lines may only be crossed to turn left to enter or leave the highway, such as into a driveway.

questions.question: An intersection has a stop sign and a crosswalk, but no stop line. You must stop:
options: Before the crosswalk
50 feet before the intersection
Where you think the stop line would be
With your front wheels in the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Without a stop line, you must stop before entering the crosswalk.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
options: Road hazard sign
Interstate route site
School crossing sign
Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs, alerting drivers to hazards or special conditions ahead.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:
options: Always come to a full stop at the intersection
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary
Look both ways as you cross the intersection
Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching
questions.explanation: A Yield sign means decrease speed, prepare to stop, and yield the right-of-way — a full stop is only required if traffic conditions call for it.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey over the other three?
options: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light
questions.explanation: Directions given by a traffic officer take precedence over any sign, signal, or pavement marking.
